# ASP.NET Core Web Hardening (WEB)

Rules for .NET web applications and APIs that browsers can reach.

## SCS-WEB-01 Enforce HTTPS and HSTS in production

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: Production web applications MUST use HTTPS only, with HTTPS redirection and an HSTS header of at least one year. APIs SHOULD not listen on plain HTTP at all.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- app.UseHsts() outside Development, with builder.Services.AddHsts(o => { o.MaxAge = TimeSpan.FromDays(365); o.IncludeSubDomains = true; }). The default is only 30 days.
- app.UseHttpsRedirection() for browser apps; for APIs, bind Kestrel/IIS to HTTPS only, since redirects come too late for API clients.
- Add preload only after every subdomain supports HTTPS.

Verification: curl -I against production shows Strict-Transport-Security with max-age ≥ 31536000, and HTTP requests do not return data.

## SCS-WEB-02 Send security headers on every response

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: Web applications and APIs MUST send standard security response headers, and MUST NOT reveal server or framework versions in headers.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- All responses: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or no-referrer for internal apps).
- HTML responses: a Content-Security-Policy (start with default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'), rolled out in report-only mode first.
- JSON APIs: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none', and Cache-Control: no-store on authenticated or personal data responses.
- Permissions-Policy that turns off unused features (camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()).
- Remove version headers: KestrelServerOptions.AddServerHeader = false; remove Server and X-Powered-By in IIS web.config.
- ASP.NET Core has no built-in security-header middleware; use a small shared middleware or a maintained package such as NetEscapades.AspNetCore.SecurityHeaders.

Verification: Scan production URLs with a header checker (for example securityheaders.com for internet-facing sites, or curl -I).

## SCS-WEB-03 Protect cookie-authenticated requests against CSRF

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: Every state-changing request that is authenticated by a cookie (including Windows authentication) MUST be protected with an anti-forgery token. State MUST NEVER change on a GET request. Authentication cookies MUST be HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- MVC / Razor Pages: [AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken] globally, and the form tag helper (which adds the token automatically).
- Minimal APIs: endpoints that bind forms require a token once antiforgery is enabled. JSON endpoints under cookie auth are not validated automatically; add an endpoint filter that calls IAntiforgery.IsRequestValidAsync for unsafe methods.
- Cookies: HttpOnly = true, SecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.Always, SameSite = Strict (or Lax), a __Host- name prefix, and a short expiry.
- SameSite is defense in depth only. Bearer-token APIs (the mobile apps) do not need antiforgery.

Verification: Submit a cross-site form or a request without the token and expect HTTP 400.

## SCS-WEB-04 Configure hosts, proxies and caching safely

Level: SHOULD

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: Web applications SHOULD restrict allowed host names, trust forwarded headers only from known proxies, build absolute links from configured values, and never cache one user's data for another.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Set AllowedHosts to the real host names (not "*").
- ForwardedHeaders: set KnownProxies (or KnownIPNetworks on .NET 10). Never clear them, and do not set ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED=true.
- Build password-reset and confirmation links from a configured public base URL, never from Request.Host.
- Place UseOutputCache after UseAuthentication/UseAuthorization, and never send Cache-Control: public on user data.

Verification: Send a request with a forged Host or X-Forwarded-For header and confirm it is rejected or ignored.
